messages:
Priya R: Heads up — since the runtime merge yesterday (w/ the matmul heuristic tweak) we're seeing a persistent p95 decode regression on long-chat workloads. Canary jobs + a few customer traces show ~2x tail. Anyone bisected yet?

Alex C: Yep seeing it on our canaries. p50 unchanged, tail jumps on sequences >1024. Flamegraph points to `matmul_transpose` kernel occupying most of the decode tail. :eyes:

Maya S: Also noticed KV cache eviction counts spiked ~3x for the same time window (same fleets). Eviction rate graph attached to the monitoring alert. Could be related (more cache churn -> more decode work).

Josh L: Quick bisect locally: revert of the matmul-selection heuristic patch brings p95 back to baseline. Repro steps: checkout runtime@HEAD~1, build, run `./perf/run_decode_longseq --seed=42`. With HEAD: p95=210ms, with revert: p95=98ms. Commit that flips behavior is `abcdef1` (heuristic: prefer_transpose=true).

infra-bot: CI perf job `decode-longseq` failed at 2024-06-15T09:12:30Z (job id 2247). Regression flagged: p95 +32% vs baseline. Link: https://ci.redwood/workflows/2247

Priya R: Can we get a short triage: is the cause kernel choice (matmul_transpose) interacting with fused-attn fallback or KV behavior? Or is it purely matmul kernel perf mismatch for long sequences?

Alex C: Looking at traces, when matmul_transpose is chosen we see more KV evictions during decode (likely because throughput changes timing and cache gets invalidated sooner). Also observed some cases where the fused-attn codepath falls back to an unfused path because the kernel selector returns a different op shape ordering. So two interacting regressions: kernel pick + increased cache churn.

Josh L: Posted a short bisect log snippet:```
Bisect log:
start: HEAD -> p95=210ms
good: runtime@HEAD~1 -> p95=98ms
bad commit: abcdef1
note: heuristic prefers transpose at seq>512
```

Priya R: Seems high risk to continue rollout. Propose: 1) hold canary rollout 2) revert heuristic commit until we have a robustness fix 3) add CI perf test for long-chat path + KV churn metric. Thoughts?

revert-bot: Suggested revert PR created: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/789 (revert of abcdef1). Marking as rollout-blocker.

Alex C: I'll open the revert PR properly and set canary to hold. Also going to run targeted flamegraphs across bfloat16/float16/bf16 matmul kernels — initial suspicion: matmul_transpose is significantly worse on Ampere for certain tile sizes.

Maya S: FYI we saw the eviction thrash primarily on instances that have heavy multi-tenant short-lived KV inserts (chat connectors). If kernel timing shifts cause slightly higher per-request time, it creates a feedback loop: more clients overlap -> more cache evictions -> worse tail. Adds to the argument for reverting.

Josh L: Revert PR #789 opened and is running CI. Short-term mitigation if revert delayed: lower canary qps + increase cache expiry to reduce churn. But that's brittle.

infra-bot: Revert PR #789 CI status: running perf suite (includes `decode-longseq`).

Priya R: Action items from triage: - @Alex C open+merge revert PR and hold rollout - @Josh L run perf CI on both kernels + attach flamegraphs - @Maya S gather KV eviction graphs for affected machines and add a dashboard alert - Postmortem if revert lands.

Alex C: Revert PR merged at 1719808200. Canary rollout held. Observing metrics now.

Maya S: After revert metrics: p95 back to baseline (~100ms), KV eviction rate returned to normal, no more fused-attn fallbacks. I'll attach before/after charts to the PR.

Priya R: Great — closing the immediate incident. Follow-ups: add a unit perf test that runs kernel selector on seeded shapes + add KV-churn guardrail in console to detect similar regressions earlier. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
